root_cause.text: `rcu_read_unlock_special()` could re-enter itself through `raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ)` while handling a deferred quiescent-state request because it did not mark the per-CPU RCU state as already pending before queuing the softirq, allowing an infinite recursion/deadloop after `__rcu_read_unlock()` lost its recursion protection.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kernel/rcu/tree_plugin.h` so `rcu_read_unlock_special()` now checks `rdp->defer_qs_pending`, sets it to `DEFER_QS_PENDING` before calling `raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ)`, and renames the flag from `defer_qs_iw_pending` to `defer_qs_pending`; the CVE text explicitly says the issue appears because commit `5f5fa7ea89dc` removed recursion-protection from `__rcu_read_unlock()`, enabling a deadloop in `raise_softirq_irqoff()` with ftrace enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename the pending-state field and update its comment to more accurately describe that it covers irqwork or softirq deferred quiescent-state handling.
intent_record.what: In struct rcu_data, the field named `defer_qs_iw_pending` was renamed to `defer_qs_pending`, and its comment was changed from "Scheduler attention pending?" to "irqwork or softirq pending?".
intent_record.how: This changes only the identifier and documentation for the member, making it reflect that the flag tracks pending deferred quiescent-state handling from either irqwork or softirq paths; the runtime storage and type remain unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the deferred quiescent-state handling to update the correct per-CPU pending flag in rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_irqrestore().
intent_record.what: In rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_irqrestore(), the code changes the checked and assigned per-CPU field name from `defer_qs_iw_pending` to `defer_qs_pending` in the conditional that clears a pending deferred quiescent-state flag.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the function operate on the correct state variable, so a pending deferred quiescent-state condition is properly cleared when it is set; previously the code referenced a different field name and would not update the intended flag.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the deferred quiescent-state handler to clear the correct pending state field when preemption is still active.
intent_record.what: In `rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_handler()`, the assignment inside the `if (rcu_preempt_depth() > 0)` branch was changed from writing `DEFER_QS_IDLE` to `rdp->defer_qs_iw_pending` to writing it to `rdp->defer_qs_pending`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler now updates the non-IRQ-work deferred quiescent-state pending flag instead of the IRQ-work-specific pending flag when preemption depth is still nonzero, which changes which internal state is cleared/recorded for deferred QS processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid duplicate RCU softirq wakeups by only raising the softirq when deferred quiescent-state processing is not already pending.
intent_record.what: The code in `rcu_read_unlock_special()` was changed so that `raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ);` is now executed only after checking `rdp->defer_qs_pending != DEFER_QS_PENDING`. If the flag is not already set, the code sets `rdp->defer_qs_pending = DEFER_QS_PENDING` before raising the softirq.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents repeatedly queueing the same deferred quiescent-state work and avoids redundant softirq raises when the deferred QS request is already pending. It ensures the request is marked once and only then scheduled for handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the deferred quiescent-state pending flag used when queueing IRQ work in rcu_read_unlock_special().
intent_record.what: In rcu_read_unlock_special(), the code changed the pending-state field checked and set from rdp->defer_qs_iw_pending to rdp->defer_qs_pending in the IRQ_WORK-enabled path before queueing defer_qs_iw on rdp->cpu.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the deferred quiescent-state request now uses the shared defer_qs_pending flag instead of the IRQ-work-specific pending field, so the code will correctly detect and mark an outstanding deferred QS operation before queueing the work item.

grouping_result.intent: Rename the pending-state field and update its comment to more accurately describe that it covers irqwork or softirq deferred quiescent-state handling.
Fix the deferred quiescent-state pending flag used when queueing IRQ work in rcu_read_unlock_special().
Avoid duplicate RCU softirq wakeups by only raising the softirq when deferred quiescent-state processing is not already pending.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix incorrect deferred quiescent-state pending flag handling in RCU preempt/deferred QS IRQ paths.

relevance_review.reason: The change only renames a pending-state field and clarifies its comment. It does not alter the logic that prevents re-entering rcu_read_unlock_special() or mark the per-CPU RCU state as pending before raising the softirq, which is the root cause of the recursion bug.

The changes directly target deferred quiescent-state pending flag handling in `rcu_read_unlock_special()` and related IRQ paths, which matches the root cause: the code failed to mark the per-CPU RCU state as pending before queuing the softirq, enabling re-entry and recursion.

The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents re-entering rcu_read_unlock_special()/RCU_SOFTIRQ by ensuring deferred quiescent-state processing is marked pending before raising the softirq, avoiding duplicate wakeups and recursion/deadloop.

candidates.rationale: This directly triggers the RCU softirq from rcu_read_unlock_special() without first ensuring the per-CPU deferred-QS state is marked pending, which matches the re-entry/deadloop root cause.
This shows the existing pending-flag check used in the deferred-QS path, which is part of the incorrect state handling that allowed the softirq path to be re-entered.
Clearing the deferred-QS pending state at the wrong time/using the wrong flag can leave the CPU appearing not-pending and allow repeated softirq queuing, contributing to recursion.
This guards the IRQ-work queueing path that is supposed to prevent repeated deferred-QS scheduling; the vulnerability arises when this path fails to correctly reflect already-pending work.
Queueing deferred quiescent-state work without the proper pending-state marking is the mechanism that can repeatedly reinvoke the handling path and lead to the observed recursion.

vuln_statements.explanation: This directly queues the RCU softirq from rcu_read_unlock_special() without first marking the deferred quiescent-state work as already pending, enabling re-entry into rcu_read_unlock_special() and the recursion/deadloop described in the root cause.

This queues deferred quiescent-state irq work on the CPU, and in the vulnerable logic it could be re-queued without the correct pending-state update, allowing repeated reinvocation of the handling path and the resulting recursion.

This is the conditional guarding the irq-work queueing path in rcu_read_unlock_special(); the bug is in the path that should prevent duplicate deferred-QS scheduling but failed to set the pending state before queueing.
